approach: Weighted scoring model (primary, explainable) + K-Means clustering (k=3) for tiering
known_limitations: Unsupervised scoring - there is no ground-truth 'correct' supplier ranking to validate against; validation relies on internal cluster quality, cross-method agreement, and resampling stability instead of accuracy.
Only 12 suppliers - clustering metrics (silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz) are inherently less stable at this sample size than they would be with dozens of suppliers.
Suppliers with fewer than 150 orders (see low_confidence_suppliers) have noisier aggregate metrics and their tier assignment should be treated as provisional.
Trained on one year of simulated order data; supplier performance in reality can drift, so periodic re-scoring is required, not a one-time classification.
retraining_recommendation: Recompute quarterly as new orders accumulate, and re-run the bootstrap stability check each time - a supplier whose stability_pct drops sharply between runs is worth investigating before trusting its new tier.
